items.title: The majority of Tuvalu has applied to relocate to Australia to escape climate change. What happens now?
items.description: Tuvalu is building new land to hold back rising sea levels, but the majority of its people are applying to relocate to Australia. As they do, many are confronting a disturbing question.

items.title: Results are out for the world's most powerful company, but investors aren't impressed
items.description: The world's most valuable company, tech giant Nvidia, has reported a record revenue but investors are not impressed with second-quarter sales forecasts.

items.title: Live: Local share market up on news unemployment rate has increased
items.description: The unemployment rate has increased by 0.2 percentage points in April, to 4.5 per cent (in seasonally adjusted terms). A drop in female employment drove the overall fall. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Live: Paul Keating backs CGT changes as 'structurally sound'
items.description: Former prime minister Paul Keating says the government's changes to capital gains tax are "structurally sound" and seek to "arrest" the growth in house prices. Follow live.

items.title: Musk's X ordered to pay fine for failing to comply with child protection request
items.description: Elon ​Musk's social media company X Corp has ​admitted ‌to not complying with an order from Australia's eSafety commissioner to ⁠provide information about the measures it has in place ​to stop ‌child exploitation on the X platform.

items.title: 'Survival mode all the time': Australian parents break taboos on raising kids
items.description: As the birth rate hits a record low it's been revealed that almost 60 per cent of Australian parents are experiencing psychological distress, according to the largest-ever national parenting survey.

items.title: Woman dies after being hit by police car in Cairns
items.description: A 71-year-old woman has died after being hit by a police car in Cairns on Thursday morning.

items.title: Breaking: Queensland Olympics Minister referred to AFP over voting registration
items.description: The Australian Electoral Commission (AEC) confirmed on Thursday it had made the referral.

items.title: As Colbert wraps up The Late Show, late-night TV could be on shaky ground
items.description: Like other checks and balances on presidential power, late-night talk shows — once ratings juggernauts, woven into the fabric of American culture — are being stress-tested. Here's how they became a staging ground for the battle over free speech.

items.title: 'Suspicious' item that saw Avalon Airport evacuated was hair removal device
items.description: A person was arrested after an item was declared suspicious item during security screening at the airport early this morning.

items.title: This election just tested Trump's sway over the Republican Party
items.description: Donald Trump's revenge tour is in full swing, and his latest victim is a Republican who has voted with his party more than 90 per cent of the time.

items.title: British plane swooped by Russian fighter jets over Black Sea
items.description: Two Russian jets have intercepted a Royal Air Force plane over the Black Sea, flying close enough to trigger its emergency systems.

items.title: Students return to high school as police revoke emergency declaration
items.description: Police have revoked an emergency declaration under the Public Safety Preservation Act after a Cairns high school was evacuated following reports of a threat.

items.title: Why 70,000 people could decide future for 70 million Brits
items.description: Andy Burnham is angling to become the UK's next prime minister. He has plenty of popularity, but no seat in parliament. That could be about to change.

items.title: What are the signs of broken heart syndrome?
items.description: Experts say broken heart syndrome accounts for about two per cent of patients presenting with symptoms similar to a heart attack.

items.title: How to improve your home without stepping inside
items.description: Adding a new kitchen or bathroom to your home can be expensive, but budget constraints don't mean you have to take home improvement off the table altogether.

items.title: Think you know music and film? Let's see how well you score in this quiz
items.description: From Mozart to Max Richter, can you pick the classical music in these iconic films?

items.title: Pressure builds on new homes and inflation as costs go through the roof
items.description: Amid fast-rising prices — from materials craned in, to rubbish trucked out — a residential builder lists the costlier surcharges, levies and products hammering the construction industry and fuelling inflation.

items.title: Gen Zs who approach share market like 'lottery ticket' could pay more tax
items.description: Gen Zs who take a lottery ticket approach to investing in the stock market will likely pay more tax under the capital gains tax changes being proposed by the government.

items.title: Labor burns political capital as tax reform backlash grows
items.description: In an already difficult post-budget week, Labor isn't being helped by some of its "friends". But it has won an important endorsement from one powerful voice.

items.title: Photographer accused of stealing Bondi terror attack victim's camera
items.description: A photographer who allegedly stole a camera from a Bondi terror attack victim before pawning it days later has been charged.

items.title: NRL star Arrow reveals MND has already affected his speech
items.description: Jai Arrow reveals that MND has already affected his speech after announcing yesterday he was stepping away from the NRL after his shock diagnosis.

items.title: Prince William goes wild in crowd as Aston Villa ends 30-year drought
items.description: In front of a joyful future king of England, Aston Villa coach Unai Emery reaffirmed his status as the king of the Europa League as Villa beat Freiburg 3-0 in Istanbul to secure Emery a record-extending fifth title in the Europa League.

items.title: Snowtown killer James Vlassakis's image has been revealed. Here's why
items.description: The youngest of the Snowtown killers was the subject of a long-running suppression order that kept his face — or any description of his appearance — hidden for 25 years. Here's why that's been lifted.

items.title: Older Australians anxiously waiting months for Support at Home invoices
items.description: Some advocates say the government's decision to delay price caps for at-home aged care services is a "burden".
